problem: Prior audio-based navigation work treats audio only as an auxiliary modality to vision, and speaker localization/detection methods cannot directly control an agent that must reach a target speaker while avoiding others.
motivation: Audio-only navigation is barely studied in RL, yet humans can navigate by listening. The paper asks whether an agent can learn from raw stereo audio alone to identify a target speaker among several and move to it while avoiding the interfering speakers.
key_idea: Train a small PPO policy end-to-end on raw concatenated stereo waveform frames in a Unity 2D room to navigate to a target speaker while avoiding distractor speakers.
insight: The raw-waveform MLP policy learns implicit speaker identification and direction cues from stereo volume differences, and reaches 98% success against 15% for a random agent. It still reaches 78% when trained on a single utterance per speaker, and 93% under 4-8% pitch shift never seen in training. These results suggest the agent learns fairly robust speaker representations. There are no further ablations, and no comparison to non-RL or audio-visual baselines.
method: Agent network: MLP with two 256-unit hidden layers; outputs a 2-D continuous velocity (vx, vy) in [-1,1].
Input: the last 1024 samples per channel (~21 ms at 48 kHz) of left and right stereo audio from Unity, concatenated into a 2048-dim vector.

Environment: Unity 2D room with 3 stationary speakers (one target TS, two distractors S1 and S2) playing random utterances. Volume rolls off linearly with distance and all sources are audible everywhere in the room.
Reward: +1 for reaching the target; -1 for hitting a distractor or leaving the room; -0.001 per step. The episode ends on any of these.
Training: PPO with GAE-style advantage, gamma=0.99, c1=0.95, c2=0.001, clip epsilon=0.2; 6M steps; agent and speakers start at random positions.
Data: about 600 utterances per speaker from 3 audiobooks (VAD-segmented, manually corrected), split about 500 train / 100 test per speaker.

setting.backbone: 2-layer MLP (256-256) trained from scratch with PPO
setting.model_size: small MLP (~0.6M params, estimated from the architecture)
setting.training_data: about 500 audiobook utterances per speaker (3 speakers), 6M RL steps in the Unity environment; no extra data
setting.observation: raw stereo audio waveform (2x1024 samples), no vision

numbers.eval_set_note: 100 test episodes per target speaker, averaged over 3 target-speaker choices; test utterances held out from training
numbers.evidence: Our agent is able to successfully reach the target speaker in 98 out of 100 played episodes (98% success rate)... random agent is 15%

numbers.eval_set_note: trained on only 1 utterance per speaker, tested on the full test set
numbers.evidence: when trained on the minimal training set of just 1 utterance per speaker it has a 78% success rate
the success rate only exhibits a modest drop from 98% to 93%

numbers_note: Results are given mainly in a figure and in the text; numbers are taken from the text. The benchmark is a custom Unity environment.
results: The PPO agent reaches the target speaker in 98% of test episodes versus 15% for a random-walk agent. With only 1 training utterance per speaker it still achieves 78%, and under 4-8% pitch shift it achieves 93%.
limitations: Very simple environment: a single empty room, 3 stationary speakers, no walls or occlusion acoustics, and volume audible everywhere.
Only a random-policy baseline; no comparison against other methods, and the result is on a custom Unity task with 100 test episodes per target speaker.
Only 3 speakers, and a separate agent is trained per target speaker; not evaluated on unseen speakers or real audio.
